idiom_name: Fluent @Group over a Fields struct stored flat in the owner's table
implementation_notes: Fluent realizes Embedded Value with @Group: a struct conforming to Fields (which may itself contain @Field, @Enum or another @Group) is stored as a flat structure in the owner's table with the keys joined by an underscore, so pet.name becomes pet_name - the pattern's decomposition, with the prefix supplied by the group's key. Unlike a Codable struct stored in a single @Field, the fields of a @Group remain queryable through dot syntax on the property wrappers, which is the difference between Embedded Value and Serialized LOB in this framework. The value stays a plain struct with no identifier, which is what the pattern requires.
pitfalls: Fluent's @Group keys are joined with an underscore, so two groups whose keys prefix one another (pet and pet_details) can produce colliding column names.
A nested Codable struct in a single @Field is not the same thing: it is stored as one value and its fields cannot be filtered, which turns the pattern into a Serialized LOB.
Models must have an empty initializer and are classes, so the value type must not be a reference type if you want value semantics - use a struct conforming to Fields.
